Michael,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement ran the draft order form by our finance team and they raised a concern about the step changes between volume slabs in Exhibit B — when usage moves from one slab to the next our expected spend can jump materially month-to-month. They asked whether Redwood can include a short transition mechanism (a smoothing amortization or prorated transition over the remaining quarter) and a simpler quarterly true-up rather than immediate per-invoice reprice.

Can your team propose language or an exhibit to make the transition less spiky? We want to avoid long-term minimums but also need predictability for forecasting. Attaching the order form you sent.

- Kirsten
CloudMetrics — Sr. Procurement Manager

Kirsten —

Really appreciate the clear ask. We can do a couple of approaches: (1) a 30/60/90-day step-down smoothing where price blends between slabs over the calendar quarter, or (2) a quarterly true-up that applies the higher slab retroactively to the quarter-end usage with a credit mechanism to soften mid-quarter invoices. Both preserve your forecasting while protecting Redwood from short bursts.

I'll draft an Exhibit that shows the math and a clean clause for the order form. Copying our legal and sales lead to scope the language and confirm revenue math.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Team —

Reviewed the ask and attached exhibit. Legal preference is for a quarterly true-up with an explicit transition exhibit because: (a) it is easier to audit, (b) it avoids month-to-month provisional credits that complicate invoicing, and (c) it cleanly limits our liability.

Proposed clause (insert into Order Form, Exhibit D — "Volume Transition and True-up"):
"During each Quarter, Customer will be invoiced at the applicable slab rate for Consumption during the then-current billing period. Within thirty (30) days after the end of each Quarter Redwood shall calculate actual Consumption for the Quarter and apply a true-up as follows: if Customer's actual Quarterly Consumption falls into a higher pricing slab than was billed during the Quarter, Redwood shall issue an invoice for the delta at the higher slab rate (the \"True-Up Invoice\"). If the True-Up Invoice results in a net credit to Customer, Redwood shall apply such credit to the next invoice. Any True-Up Invoice will be payable within thirty (30) days. For avoidance of doubt, Redwood's cumulative refunds or credits for a Quarter shall not exceed the aggregate charges for that Quarter."

Two additional commercial guardrails: (1) a smoothing cap that limits the True-Up Invoice to X% of the average monthly invoice for the preceding Quarter (we recommend 50% as starting point), and (2) a 180-day audit/lookback right for Redwood to recalculate usage where systematic underreporting is suspected.

I attached a redline (OrderForm_Redline_20270216.pdf) with the clause inserted and a short worked example table. If Sales wants the blending option instead, we can draft a blending table, but operationally the quarterly true-up is simpler.

- Neha
Neha Kapoor
